| Hello Forward Friends- Happy Halloween! I hope everyone takes a little break from all the craziness going on and enjoys themselves safely tonight. I also hope everyone who has local elections this year and hasn't cast their ballot yet makes it out to vote on Tuesday. I am so appreciative to everyone who has signed up to be part of our [national volunteer program](https://home.forwardparty.com/volunteer?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_oct_3&n=2), and I am excited to share a full calendar for November at the end of this message! We are in full swing reaching out to our elected officials, text banking, and calling new supporters. Please check the calendar to find an event to attend if you've signed up for a program. We at Forward are concerned for the millions of families who might be affected by the government shutdown and struggle to put food on the table and obtain other basic necessities this month. We will be organizing food drives in as many states as possible. Please stay tuned for more information, and reply to this email if you would like to help organize one in your area. _Volunteer Spotlight:_ Congratulations to **Nate Roseboro** in New Jersey! He has spent all year working hard to get candidates in his state, and he has been doing an excellent job as co chair for the [Black Voters Committee](https://home.forwardparty.com/black_voters_committee?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_oct_3&n=3). We know we can count on Nate to get things done, and we appreciate him! _Upcoming events:_ **Mon Nov 3rd @ 7pm ET** \- our last [Monday Night Madness](https://home.forwardparty.com/monday_night_madness_text_banking_20251103?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_oct_3&n=4) text banking event before the election. Please help us GOTV! **Wed Nov 5th @ 630pm ET** \- Week 3 of our [Elected official outreach series](https://home.forwardparty.com/elected_official_outreach_series_jp4xyksaiasn_sr6zxgkw_20251105?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_oct_3&n=5)\- tracking and follow up! **Thurs Nov 6th @ 5:30pm CT** \- [Illinois statewide call](https://home.forwardparty.com/illinois_statewide_call?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_oct_3&n=6) **Mon Nov 10th @ 530pm CT** \- our first [Alabama statewide call!](https://home.forwardparty.com/al_statewide_call?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_oct_3&n=7) **Thurs Nov 13th @ 7pm ET** \- [Georgia statewide call](https://home.forwardparty.com/ga_fwd_statewide_call_20251113?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_oct_3&n=8) Find more and in-person events on our [calendar](https://home.forwardparty.com/public_calendar?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_oct_3&n=9)! If your state doesn't have a statewide call and you would like to help host one, please reply to this email and let me know. Thanks for reading. I hope you have a wonderful weekend! Carrie Anne Templeton

name: Eric Sorensen (personal)
subject: Before your trick-or-treating:
body:
Peter,
I’m glad I could catch you around your Halloween plans.
Tonight marks our October end-of-month fundraising deadline.
We haven’t been fundraising much during Trump’s shutdown of the government, and at the moment, we’re hoping to make a late splash to keep our operation funded. Will you rush in a donation before midnight to help us meet this monthly benchmark?
Here’s a good link: [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/es-q4-2025](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/118414713/579677442/795475316?refcode=em-10.31.25-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMzk1Nzc4Ny05ZGI2LWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=GGEWpT2mlRvc8UFrXrt8H7EF0uMZsTgdvnUeYLe-kC0=)
I’ll be spending my evening passing out candy – and maybe I’ll meet (and sway) a few voters at my doorstep!
Right now, the scariest thing isn’t a ghoul or a goblin, but Republicans’ complete disregard for the Constitution and the people they’re sworn to serve.

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

Hi, it’s Tobias Read, Oregon Secretary of State.
Tonight’s the deadline. We set a goal of $20,000 by Oct 31, and here’s why it matters — not in abstractions, but in line items. (If you already understand the stakes, you can click here to donate before midnight.) [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=251031em]
First, we fortify the front door of democracy: voter privacy. If the federal government demands sensitive data again, we need counsel ready to file — immediately — and the capacity to notify voters about what’s at stake and how we’re protecting them.
Second, we keep the engine room running: local elections. That means overtime and back-up staffing; replacement ballot stock and verified envelopes; secure transport runs from drop sites; and on-call tech support when tabulators work late.
Third, we protect the information commons: a rapid-response team to debunk false claims about vote-by-mail, publish verified guidance in multiple languages, and push real-time updates when bad actors try to sow confusion about ballots or drop boxes in Portland and beyond.
Every dollar tonight moves one of those levers. That’s how we translate Oregon values into Oregon outcomes.
Trump can attack Portland with insults. He can try to intimidate voters with lawsuits and threats. But he doesn’t get to decide who participates in our elections — you do.
If you believe Oregon should answer to its people, not to bullies, I need you with me in these final hours.
Please rush a donation of any amount right now to help me hit my $20,000 fundraising goal tonight by midnight. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=251031em]

name: Gary Miller for House of Delegates
subject: "Hope is a discipline" - A lesson from a 102-year-old Virginian
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY GARY MILLER FOR DELEGATE** 121 Bell Ct
body:
In the final days of a long campaign, it’s easy to feel cynical.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://us9.campaign-archive.com/?e=606d7e9aa2&u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=7c02d264ff)
---
[|
---](https://drmillerforyou.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=f0b896ce81&e=606d7e9aa2)
| | | | |
---
| |

Friend,
In the final days of a long campaign, it’s easy to feel cynical. It's easy to believe the noise that says your voice doesn't matter, that the system is rigged, and that nothing will ever really change.
**Hope is the discipline of showing up** , even when you're tired.It is the discipline of believing in common sense, even when it's unpopular, and it is the discipline of casting a vote, even when the outcome isn't guaranteed.
[This is Ms. **Edith Edmunds of Halifax**. She is 102 years old. She is a quilting master, a community elder, and a true Virginia treasure.](https://drmillerforyou.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=be33682a6d&e=606d7e9aa2)
She has also voted in **every single election since 1948.**
I had the profound honor of sitting with her, and I asked her why. Why, for over 75 years, has she never missed one?
Her answer must be heard across the Commonwealth.
[**"I vote to let them know that I'm human. And I can think just like you... Whether the person I voted for wins or not, I vote."**](https://drmillerforyou.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=00e068a66b&e=606d7e9aa2)
This is the very definition of disciplined hope.
It is the act of showing up, not because victory is certain, but because participation is essential. It's the profound understanding that our humanity and our voice are linked, and that **we must exercise that voice to affirm our place in our community**.
This is the Virginia I am fighting for.
I am not running on cynicism. I am running on the common-sense belief that we, the people, can still solve our own problems.
We can lower your electric bills by **breaking up the monopolies** , and we can create **new paths to the middle class** by investing in skilled trades and technical education. We must restore common sense to Richmond.
[None of it is possible without that same discipline Ms. Edmunds has shown us.](https://drmillerforyou.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=fd80ac7017&e=606d7e9aa2)
We are **4 days away** from Election Day. This is our moment to choose action over apathy. This is our time to practice the discipline of hope.
**Please, make your plan to vote on Tuesday, November 4th.**
Vote for common sense. Vote to honor the legacy of voters like Ms. Edmunds. **Vote to let them know that** _**you**_**are here.**
Thank you for your support,
Dr. Gary MillerDemocratic Nominee House of Delegates - 49

subject: The Mountain Minute: 10/31/2025 🎃
body:
The Real “Trick or Treat” in D38, plus more on Durango schools
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Happy Halloween, friends! 🎃
Stay safe out there tonight, friends. And we heard through the grapevine there maybe riots starting tonight with those [upset about SNAP benefits](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Confirmed that there's already been violence in Pueblo last night at a local Walmart.
🎤 **Day 8** of the **Douglas County Dirty Dozen is out.** When schools ignore warning signs, kids pay the price. A sixth-grade teacher accused of grooming students was left in classrooms for years — even after red flags. 🚩🚩🚩
Watch the latest video and follow along on [X](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), [Instagram](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), [Facebook](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) & [TikTok](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)!
Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Legal battles and social flashpoints defined the week. A federal judge is weighing whether [ICE’s warrantless arrests in Colorado](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) violated due process, while Attorney General Phil Weiser [sued to keep U.S. Space Command](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in the state, calling its planned move to Alabama politically retaliatory. As SNAP benefits near expiration amid the federal shutdown, state officials are urging swift action to [protect 225,000 residents](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) relying on food and healthcare aid. Meanwhile, a parental rights group wants lawmakers to [overturn a 2024 competency law](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) they say lets violent criminals back on the streets.

🇺🇸 **On the National Stage...** The shutdown fight escalated as even [The Washington Post urged Democrats to end the impasse](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), warning that SNAP funds will run out by November 1 and millions risk losing aid. The paper said the “pain point” is growing with healthcare enrollment delays and mounting public backlash, signaling Democrats may soon be forced to compromise.
🗣️ **Commentary Spotlight...** Heidi Ganahl’s Durango’s School Board Debacle details how [DEI priorities and Pride-flag politics eclipsed academics and safety](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) amid a teacher’s federal indictment, while Michael J. Badagliacco’s[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) [Conservatives Cannot Afford to Sleep on This Election](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) warns that low turnout could empower progressives and urges defending TABOR and electing reform-minded school boards. Amy Stephens calls the Lewis-Palmer D38 race a choice between [“transparency and trickery,”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) urging support for Ginger Schaaf over union-aligned Jackie Burhans, and Mike O’Donnell exposes a Fort Collins donor’s [95,000-plus micro-gifts through ActBlue](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as a cautionary tale about political “addiction” and misplaced civic energy.
This is the Mountain Minute for Friday, October 31, 2025. 👻
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[The Real “Trick or Treat” in D38](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY AMY STEPHENS, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_In Lewis-Palmer District 38, voters are being asked to choose between transparency and trickery — between a school board candidate who respects parents and one who shuts them out if they dare disagree. That’s not hyperbole. It’s the documented history of union-backed activist Jackie Burhans._
_Burhans markets herself as a champion of “parental rights.” But look closer and a pattern emerges: she defends rights only when parents share her ideology. When they don’t, she dehumanizes them — mocking, marginalizing, and labeling them, often accusing them of the very tactics she uses to silence dissent._
_We saw this in the now-infamous images from La Burla Bee, a downtown nightclub in Colorado Springs. There stands Burhans — holding rainbow Pride umbrellas to usher children into an “all ages” drag show complete with demonic makeup and sexualized performances._
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Durango’s School Board Debacle: Radical Rot, Predator Blind Spots, and a Herald Hug](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY HEIDI GANAHL, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Durango parents are pushing back against a school board they say prioritizes ideology over education, citing controversial bathroom policies, DEI spending, and the reinstatement of Pride and BLM flags as evidence the district has lost focus on academics and safety.
* The district spent $69,000 on one DEI training day while rejecting a charter school backed by 650 families, and a board member was fined for using district email for her political campaign—with little accountability from leadership.
* Amid backlash and a 48-count federal indictment against a former teacher accused of grooming minors, parents and reform candidates are calling for a return to transparency, academic rigor, and “common-sense leadership” in Durango schools.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[Anatomy of a Coloradan Addicted to Making Political Donations](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY MIKE O'DONNELL, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* An analysis spotlights a 79-year-old Fort Collins woman who made 95,201 political donations totaling over $540,000 between 2005 and 2024 — much of it during the COVID lockdown — with 72% processed through ActBlue.

* The woman once averaged 57 to 78 donations per day, including nearly 30,000 donations of $1 or less and 171 rejected for insufficient funds, showing behavior akin to gambling addiction.

* ActBlue is now under investigation for possible fraud and campaign-finance violations, raising concerns that such compulsive micro-donations may reflect both individual vulnerability and systemic exploitation in political fundraising.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[While she fought cancer, a Durango teacher moved in on her child](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY JEN SCHUMANN | LOCAL | OCTOBER 29** _When Colorado mom Cindy Stein sat before state lawmakers last spring, she was still recovering from cancer—and from losing her child to a teacher’s influence in a system that no longer sees parents as essential. “While I was fighting for my life, this teacher inserted herself into my daughter’s world, convincing her to reject me and her family,” Stein told the Senate Judiciary Committee._ __****
**[The Case of Ian Roberts: A Slap in the Face to Law-Abiding Citizens](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY C. J. GARBO | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 29** _The arrest of Ian Roberts, former superintendent of Des Moines Public Schools, is more than a scandal. It is an insult to every law-abiding citizen who plays by the rules, pays their taxes, and expects their government institutions to uphold the law with fairness and integrity._ __
**[The Marxist roots of America’s racial unrest](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY MICHAEL HANCOCK | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 29** _In October 1928, the Communist International — the Moscow-based command center for global revolution — issued an extraordinary directive. Buried in the archives of the Political Secretariat of the Communist International, the document was titled “Resolution on the Negro Question in the United States.” It did not read like a humanitarian plea to end racial injustice. It read like a military plan.
_

Every First Family since has kept the spooky spirit alive.

| Hey there, it’s Governor Wes Moore. The Voter Protection Project said I could reach out with an update.

U.S. Senator Katie Britt, R-Alabama, has joined her Senate colleagues Josh Hawley, R-Missouri, and Richard Blumenthal, D-Connecticut, in introducing the Guidelines for User Age-verification and Responsible Dialogue (GUARD) Act—new legislation aimed at safeguarding minors from dangers associated with the use of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots.

The senators announced the bill’s introduction at a press conference on Wednesday, where they were joined by parents of children who committed suicide or suffered from self-harm at the direct prompting of AI chatbots.

U.S. Senator Katie Britt, R-Alabama, has joined a bipartisan coalition of Senate colleagues in launching the new Senate Stewardship Caucus. The caucus, co-chaired by Senators Tim Sheehy, R-Montana, and Martin Heinrich, D-New Mexico, will look to expand and protect access to public lands, “promote commonsense land management policies,” and “support economic growth in rural communities.”

“I’m grateful to be part of founding the bipartisan Nature Caucus and represent Alabama the Beautiful,” Britt said in an official statement Wednesday. “Our great state is not only a destination for countless sportsmen, hunters, anglers, and nature-goers, but also the proud home to hardworking famers and foresters who work diligently to feed and clothe our state, nation, and world. It’s our job as legislators to work toward responsible conservation solutions, and I’m looking forward to continuing that work as a part of this caucus to do just that.”

On Monday, the U.S. Senate voted 58-40 to confirm Alabama Supreme Court Associate Justice Bill Lewis to serve as the next U.S. District Judge for the Middle District of Alabama.

Lewis received unanimous support from Senate Republicans, with five Democrats and independent Sen. Angus King, I-ME, also voting in favor of his confirmation.

Alabama’s U.S. Sens. Katie Britt and Tommy Tuberville released public statements celebrating Lewis’s confirmation following the vote.

name: Kim Schrier (personal)
subject: I wish we had time to pause, but we simply don't.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Dr. Kim Schrier for Congress
body:
Peter,

I know these last few weeks have been tough.

The government shutdown has taken its toll on families, small businesses, and everyone just trying to get by.

It’s been frustrating to watch the dysfunction in Washington, knowing how many people are being hurt while Congress fails to do its most basic job. Even in moments like this, I remind myself why I ran for Congress in the first place: To make things work a little better for families who don't have time for political games.

And while the shutdown has slowed down just about everything in D.C., _it hasn’t slowed down this grassroots campaign._ We still have to stay ready and keep this movement in fighting shape for the people across our district and state, because that’s what next year’s election will be: a true fight for our democracy and for a brighter future. WA-08 is one of the most critical races in the country, which means we need every bit of support we can get.

I know times are hard right now, and I'm deeply appreciative of everything you do to keep this campaign strong. **But if you can spare $5, even just $1, to help me close our fundraising gap, I’d be eternally grateful. >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/schrier-october-2025](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/118418731/579691644/474981299?refcode=em25_251031_eom3un_fndd_gq_act___KS_ettx&utm_campaign=em25_251031_eom3un_fndd_gq_act___KS_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=fb4cff80-abb6-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmYjRjZmY4MC1hYmI2LWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=geZQ9dwS9CRof8QsQ7G9lMlgJ5IRweddXBJK7b9UkEc=)**

Peter,

Tomorrow, your State Senator for District 38 Greg Goode will be holding a town hall meeting in Terre Haute on redistricting. The town hall will take place from 10:30 AM ET until 1 PM ET at the Terre Haute City Hall. As there has been increased interest in the event, the Senator is asking for folks to bring their photo ID to prove they live in Senate District 38, which includes all of Vigo and Clay counties, and part of Sullivan County. Signs are not allowed.

We are encourging you to show up if you live in the district, and to state your opposition to redistricting. Even as a Republican, Senator Goode has been skeptical of redistricting, and is keeping an open mind to hear from his consituents. If you still live within Senate District 38, please attend Saturday's event if you can. We want to thank Senator Goode for listening to Hoosiers and ask him to do the right thing and vote NO on any new maps. Please remember to be respectful and keep interactions civil with the senator, his staff, and his fellow constituents.

WHERE: Terre Haute City Hall
WHEN: Saturday, November 1 from 10:30 AM-1:00 PM ET.

subject: This is unacceptable
body:

subject: I would never steal candy out of my daughters bucket (okay, maybe I did)
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CHRISTINA BOHANNAN FOR CONGRESS
body:
🎃🎃🎃🎃

| Peter,

When my daughter was little, Halloween was the day she looked forward to most. She's always had a sense of style — a little fashionista from the start — and she'd spend weeks deciding what to wear. The excitement on her face as she got ready to go out for candy with her friends was contagious.

I still remember standing on the sidewalk, watching her and all the neighborhood kids racing from house to house with their candy buckets filling up. Parents lingered by the driveways, laughing, sharing stories, and maybe — just maybe — sneaking a piece of candy or two out of the stash when their kid was distracted (guilty).

Halloween has always felt magical to me. For one night, our streets light up with porches glowing, doors open, neighbors greeting each other with warmth instead of worry. Everyone looks out for each other's kids as if they were their own. That kind of trust, that sense of connection, is what makes a neighborhood feel like home.

It's also what I believe good representation should look like. We deserve leaders who show up and see the people they serve as neighbors. **To get there, this campaign needs to stay strong through the end of the month. Quite simply, we will do as Winston Churchill said and did with the Nazis of his time, with a few edits by _your pal Cliff here_ , to bring us up to speed on where things are today:
> ...though large tracts of ~~Europe~~ _land with a 2:1 cow to 11th-grade-educated human ratio_ and many old and ~~famous~~ l _azy-ass, onetime slaveholding_ States have fallen or may fall into the grip of the Gestapo and all the odious apparatus of Nazi rule, we shall not flag or fail.
> We shall go on to the end, we shall fight in ~~France~~ Chicago, we shall fight on the ~~seas~~ _grounds of the bedbug Mar-a-Lago if we must_ , and ~~oceans~~ _to lock Pete Hegseth 's liquor cabinet_, [we shall fight with growing confidence and growing strength](https://substack.com/redirect/8286d889-e1cc-467e-b46c-3d06b6ba2a5a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ~~in the air~~ t _o stop Trump 's gaudy, Saddam-esque ballroom monstrosity_...
> we shall defend our ~~Island~~ _Constitution and neighbors_ , [whatever the cost may be, we shall fight](https://substack.com/redirect/99c73a30-203b-440b-8a64-bc01c89f2fdb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ~~on the~~ ~~beaches~~ , _Trump 's little bitches, like Stephen Miller_, we shall fight on the landing grounds, we shall fight in the fields and in the streets, we shall fight in the hills; [we shall never surrender](https://substack.com/redirect/99c73a30-203b-440b-8a64-bc01c89f2fdb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)...

Legal experts agree that those strikes are illegal extrajudicial killings — in other words, the Trump administration has murdered more than 57 people.

**When Trump deployed the National Guard into cities as part of his “war from within,” Win Without War sprang into action to defend our communities.**

What started with a mobile billboard in Washington, DC, asking troops to reflect on whether this is what they signed up for and informing them of their rights has only grown in the face of Trump’s “war from within” and out. Thanks to the amazing response from supporters like you, we were able to quickly expand our Know-Your-Rights campaign to other cities where Trump deployed troops, Chicago and Memphis, and to two major military installations, Fort Bragg and Camp Lejeune, in North Carolina.

[](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqt6QuLgQ_QmHjgIEhe1JHs78iXs7bGc4tQoGDTNHS7_nVqmYxaVJdEqJNQZ1matrPSTGcnwdqOSsj5UL5KUwt4MoLk5GufRrObYfy6QfqQO4EXcNm5eCekOV1-o24Vh_2iv8oZxynXo3WY3xFHheeRv1nP9CrImj4QMJsY-KpHFoZnklQtQx3qUGxO1tbA3oje3DaKN7xnvEjXoDJnLPQS3lAAlaFLSNnCnJuSnAEPMq3zK-tKG8APwRefExd2HRsyc5neydGBD_T4OxtVfC-kM2hVOE9Q38SvOC7un9LcSnhH7nZOsoFN15pjsTDcEIqi1j_9SusxiIO2VB18KSUAUPjzzIrdu1frQMONQN6LCmg/4l7/gQTMqqlYRFq_Qn3SwCuAFA/h3/h001.g86bWByWItfc1s6GZUJuOHznp2z_QuWM0Y45DyPHOas)

Expanding to SOUTHCOM HQ in Florida comes at a critical moment. The command is reportedly in turmoil after the admiral overseeing it abruptly announced his resignation.

Amidst a series of unauthorized, unjustified strikes against boats off the coast of Venezuela, “people are angry,” one official told The Intercept. Another said key personnel at SOUTHCOM are “disillusioned.”[1]

**Your donations can ensure more servicemembers see our resources if confronted with illegal orders.** They allow us to extend our current billboard placements even longer, intensify the frequency so that more eyes are seeing them, and expand them to even more critical locations around the country.

It’s just one of the ways we’re working to bolster the rule of law and pull us off the path toward war with Venezuela, and it’s by far the most expensive — that’s why we’re coming to you today.

**These billboards come with a lot of risk and hefty price tags, Friend. Can you help us expand our Know-Your-Rights campaign with a split donation today?**

The more money we can raise today, the more places we can put billboards up to keep this campaign going, defend our democracy, and build a safer future.

**[Our vision for a world where people live and thrive free from violence is still possible when people like us — people like you— do all we can, in ways big and small, to make it happen.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqt6QuLgQ_QmHjgIEhe1JHs78iXs7bGc4tQoGDTNHS7_neztrQfzz_BdCic9cLnrjihG6nMWtnZK0dFq3cz07DNYFjZtrUD16r1ye4RK4a9a9CtfPIQ5ST7xErP5hVpgzKVp_P04Eq4a_SaB_K_Cps8uI8AgDN7iA-PSg_uVJZA88QzYLbC_fwDnUiHfzTILQjhK2lZnUezT3EwHPM0s8e5UTuw2-aTlcoHZBXClD6MiYDaWBs81AzUn32DCK4Y4_lbeq-xpqSnM8eMz3a-Ne-Ix028lpqasgC25HHdJHXZ1h2ru5YioPhMXHueGj-9NRbN5O6Qmrt_0GsQy3AS0ogKwfzfpKAe3nsw_inv09DWLJQ/4l7/gQTMqqlYRFq_Qn3SwCuAFA/h4/h001.91QA3mSpqjLFbzPv3kVdwv8puz8JEOUWDwSsnSjxGtI)**

Thank you for working for peace,
The Win Without War team

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left.
